11.1.intro: Your email and text list is an audience you own. You can reach it for free, any time. Collect emails when ads are cheap, sell when ads are pricey.

steps.say: In your email app, check how big your list is, and how many were active in the last 90 days.
steps.check: You know how big your own audience is today.
steps.lost: Find your list size. Write it down.

steps.say: Set a list growth goal for the next quiet months. Example: +2,000 subscribers before October.
steps.check: You have a written goal with a date.
steps.lost: Write one number and one date.

steps.say: Plan one list-building push (a better form, a competition, or lead ads) in a month when ads are cheap.
steps.check: The push is in your calendar.
steps.lost: Pick one month. Put "list push" in your calendar.

11.2.intro: A competition (giveaway) can add thousands of subscribers fast. The prize decides if you get future buyers or just prize hunters.

steps.say: Read the four competition types in the lesson's table. Pick one.
steps.lost: Pick the first type in the table.

steps.say: Choose a prize only your kind of customer wants: your own products, or an experience linked to them.
steps.check: The prize will attract future buyers, not prize hunters.
steps.careful: Never offer a general gadget like a phone or a gift card.
steps.lost: Make the prize a bundle of your own products.

11.3.intro: A good competition has seven parts, from rules to checking who buys. The follow-up emails matter most.

steps.say: Pick the type and prize. Check your local promotion rules (some places need a permit).
steps.check: You know the competition is legal where you run it.
steps.lost: Look up your local giveaway rules.

steps.say: Build the entry form on a store page, and as a pop-up.
steps.check: People can enter on your site two ways.

steps.say: Make the content: a prize picture, a short video, and clear steps to enter.
steps.lost: Take one nice photo of the prize.

steps.say: Run ads to broad audiences with a Leads campaign, or a Sales campaign that sends people to the entry page.
steps.check: Ads are live and entries are coming in.

steps.say: Set up a welcome flow for people who enter, with a small offer.
steps.check: Every person who enters gets welcome emails.
steps.lost: Turn on a welcome flow for entrants.

steps.say: After the draw, announce the winner. Send everyone else a "sorry you didn't win" offer.
steps.check: Non-winners get a reason to buy.
steps.lost: Send one "sorry you didn't win" email.

steps.say: Measure the cost per email, and how many entrants buy within 90 days.
steps.check: You know if you should run another one.
steps.lost: Divide ad spend by new emails. That's cost per email.

11.4.intro: Growing your list pays off most just before big sales, when ads get pricey. Start 6 to 10 weeks early.

steps.say: Find the date 6 to 10 weeks before your next big sale. Start a list-growth push then.
steps.check: The start date is in your calendar.
steps.lost: Count back 8 weeks from your sale. Mark it.

steps.say: Build an excitement page that teases the sale, with an early-access sign-up.
steps.check: Visitors can join an early-access list.
steps.lost: Make one page with an early-access form.

11.5.intro: Four simple moves grow your followers and customers alongside your list.

steps.say: Put a small budget (like $5 to $10 a day) behind your best free Reels.
steps.check: Your best free posts reach new people.
steps.lost: Boost your best Reel for $5 a day.

steps.say: Answer direct messages with helpful replies and product links.
steps.lost: Reply to one message with a product link.

steps.say: Turn on comment filters and blocked words. Team up with a brand whose products go well with yours.
steps.check: Comments stay clean, and you reach a partner's audience.
